correctness.rationale: For a fixed binary composition (k,n-k), splitting into positive 0/1 run lengths yields A(2s)=2*C(k-1,s-1)*C(n-k-1,s-1) and A(2s+1)=(n-2s)/s times their product. The next-row/old-row ratio h_s=k(n-k-s)/[(k-s+1)(n-k-1)] is nondecreasing along the shared support, and strictly increasing between adjacent run-pairs when k<floor(n/2); any new right-tail support has old count zero. Handle k=0 and odd central equality by complements. Finite exchangeability conditions on K, a convex mixture of fixed-composition laws, so balanced tails dominate. Direct three-color exact suffix recurrence gives old (3,1,4) counts at r=7,8 of 60,14 and new (2,2,4) of 120,24, a negative minor -240; the recurrence exhausts all positive 3-color balancing moves for n<=7 and proves the first obstruction at n=8. The boundary restriction to three positive classes and elementary balancing is essential.
residual_risks: The finite cutoff is exhaustive only for the explicitly positive, three-symbol, one-unit balancing class; nothing about zero counts or larger alphabets.
